name.help: Display name for this Gmail communication channel.

client_id.help: Google OAuth client ID with Gmail API send permissions.

client_secret.help: Google OAuth client secret. Stored encrypted at rest.

from_address.help: Gmail user address used as the API sender.

from_name.help: Optional display name for the From header.

subject_prefix.help: Optional prefix added to every notification subject.

title: Gmail notification delivery
subtitle: Plugin-owned
description: This plugin owns the Gmail. It stores Gmail API settings on the channel itself and does not use the removed host email-server surface.
securityDescription: The client secret is stored encrypted at rest. Use a dedicated Google Cloud OAuth client and restrict access to Gmail API send permissions.
testDescription: The host test action sends a real email through this Gmail channel. Use a test recipient first if your mailbox reaches an on-call list.
secretKeepHint: Leave blank to keep the stored value.

step1.body: Create or choose a Google Cloud project dedicated to McHarbor notification delivery.

step2.body: Enable the Gmail API for that project and create OAuth client credentials for the sender integration.

step3.body: Grant the client Gmail send permissions and <warn>keep the client secret limited to McHarbor administrators</warn>.

step4.body: Set From address to the Gmail user that will send notifications. Some Google Workspace policies require this address to be a verified or delegated sender.

step5.body: Add one or more comma-separated recipients. Start with a test mailbox, then switch to your operations or on-call distribution list once delivery is confirmed.

step6.body: Optionally set Subject prefix, for example [McHarbor Prod], so alerts are easy to filter in mail clients and ticketing systems.

step7.body: Save the channel and click Test connection. The plugin sends a real test email through the same Gmail API path used for live workflow, alert, and backup events.

step8.body: If Test fails with an OAuth error, verify the client ID, client secret, Gmail API enablement, sender mailbox, and Workspace policy for API mail sending.
